pages.lesson:
LESSON: EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION BY THE END OF THE SUB-STRAND, LISTENING

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What makes us sad?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use non-verbal cues in oral communication to express feelings and experiences
2. show appreciation of others’ feelings as they share their experiences Core-competences to be developed: Communication and Collaboration: learners share feelings and experiences

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. use non-verbal cues in oral communication to express feelings and experiences
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to use non-verbal cues in oral communication to express feelings and experiences. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. show appreciation of others’ feelings as they share their experiences Core-competences to be developed: Communication and Collaboration: learners share feelings and experiences
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to show appreciation of others’ feelings as they share their experiences Core-competences to be developed: Communication and Collaboration: learners share feelings and experiences. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING.
2. Explain Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING.
4. Show that you can: use non-verbal cues in oral communication to express feelings and experiences
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand, LISTENING. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: What makes us sad?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. use non-verbal cues in oral communication to express feelings and experiences
2. show appreciation of others’ feelings as they share their experiences Core-competences to be developed: Communication and Collaboration: learners share feelings and experiences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
